flags.title: US Nationals, Not US Citizens — Most Significant Status Anomaly in Registry
flags.summary: American Samoans are born as US nationals — NOT US citizens. Cannot vote in any US election. Cannot hold certain federal civil service positions. Must naturalize to become a citizen. Federal benefit eligibility varies by program. Fitisemanu v. United States (2021) briefly held birthright citizenship, reversed on appeal.

flags.title: No Unemployment Insurance Program — Only US Jurisdiction Without UI
flags.summary: American Samoa has NO unemployment insurance program — federal or territorial. Workers who lose jobs have no UI safety net. Route to fa'asamoa community support networks and DHSS emergency assistance: 684-633-1187.

flags.title: Fa'asamoa — Communal Land and Matai System Provides Invisible Safety Net
flags.summary: Fa'asamoa (the Samoan way): communal land ownership (90%+ land communally owned, cannot be sold to non-Samoans), matai (chiefly title holders) govern family affairs and land access, village council (fono) governance. This system provides food, housing, child care, elder support that does not appear in formal registries. At intake, ask about family and village support specifically.

flags.title: EEOC Coverage — Contested Jurisdiction, Verify Before Filing
flags.summary: EEOC jurisdiction over American Samoa has been legally contested. Title VII does not explicitly name American Samoa. Contact EEOC Honolulu (808-541-3118) to confirm current enforcement position before filing any charge.

flags.title: Medicaid Block Grant — Smallest Federal Health Grant in Registry
flags.summary: American Samoa's Medicaid equivalent is block-granted with the smallest federal health grant in the registry. Provider network extremely limited. LBJ Tropical Medical Center (684-633-1222) is the only hospital — medical evacuation to Hawaii for complex cases.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: American Samoa Emergency Hold
flags.message: AS involuntary psychiatric hold law: American Samoa Emergency Hold. Statutory authority: AS Rev. Stat. § 13.0801. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in AS retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in AS: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: American Samoa Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: American Samoa Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
